title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 436
paragraphs: Now while Cambyses was marching against Egypt, the Lacedemonians had also made an expedition against Samos and against Polycrates son of Aiakes, who had risen up against the government and gained power over Samos. At first he had divided the state into three parts and given a share to his brothers Pantagnotos and Syloson; but afterwards he put one of them to death, and drove out the younger, Syloson, and so obtained possession of all Samos. Then, being in possession, he made a guest-friendship with Amasis king of Egypt, sending him gifts and receiving gifts in return. After this, within a short period, the power of Polycrates increased rapidly, and there was much fame of it not only in Ionia but also over the rest of Hellas: for wherever he directed his forces, everything went fortunately for him. He had gotten for himself a hundred fifty-oared galleys and a thousand archers, and he plundered all men indiscriminately, making no distinction; for he used to say that he would earn more gratitude from a friend by giving back what he had taken than by not taking at all. So he had conquered many of the islands and many cities on the mainland, and besides other things he won a sea-fight against the Lesbians as they were coming with their forces to aid the Milesians, and defeated them; and these men dug the whole trench round the wall of the city of Samos while working in chains.
